procedural_matters: Hearing No. 24 was heard together with hearing No. 27 in accordance with RRS 63.2(b) since both hearings arose from the same incident.
TUR 97 was represented by Ozlem Irmak Tomak (helm).
NZL 28 was represented by Will Mason (crew).
The panel of the international jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b)
TUR 97 presented video evidence of the incident.
Howard Elliott (member of the international jury) gave evidence as a witness.
Tessa Clinton (helm of NZL 28), Jenny Armstrong (coach of NZL 28), Efe Ozgenc (crew of TUR 97) and Sergen Birincioglu (coach of TUR 97) attended the hearing as observers.
facts: The conditions at the time of the incident were 7-8 knots of wind with choppy water. The course for Mixed Dinghy (470) was an Outer Trapezoid course.
While rounding mark 2, TUR 97 touched the mark and after rounding it, she took a One-Turn Penalty, beginning with a gybe and then tacking onto starboard tack.
When TUR 97 reached a close-hauled course, NZL 28 was rounding the mark. At that moment, both boats were on a bow-to -ow collision course at a distance of one boat length.
NZL 28 bore away to a broad reach and sailed to starboard of TUR 97, who was bearing away continuously.
When TUR 97’s bow was aiming at the port aft quarter of NZL 28, NZL 28 gybed onto port tack.
Immediately after, TUR 97 luffed sharply and and passed less than one metre astern of NZL 28.
conclusions: When changing course, TUR 97, the right-of-way boat, gave NZL 28 room to keep clear, as required by RRS 16.1.
NZL 28 on port-tack failed to keep clear of TUR 97 on starboard-tack, and broke RRS 10.
Since NZL 28 broke RRS 10 while she was sailing within the room to which she was entitled, she is exonerated under RRS 43.1(b) for this breach.
decision: Protest upheld. Since NZL 28 is exonerated by RRS 43.1(b) for her breach of RRS 10, no penalty is imposed on NZL 28.
